changed.title: At least 2n gates for n distinct half-size rows read once by ORs on the one-a-side promise in fan-in-two AND/OR circuits
changed.statement:
∀ (n k : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin (2 * k) → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  2 ≤ k →
  Function.Injective G →
  (∀ u, (Finset.univ.filter (fun c => G u c = true)).card = k) →
  (∀ c, ∃ v, G v c = false) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + 2 * k) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  (∀ x : Fin n,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.size) x.val = 1 ∧
    ∃ (j : Fin C.gates.length) (s : ℕ),
      (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∧
      ((C.gates.get j).inputs = [x.val, s] ∨ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [s, x.val])) →
  2 * n ≤ C.size
changed.unlocks: the count behind names against literals in its general form, two gates a row when every row is read once by an OR, for the line of what a row costs on the one-a-side promise
changed.context: On paper. Each row has a private OR. Distinct half-size neighborhoods are incomparable, so domination prevents one row OR from reading another. Charge two half-slots to two readers, or a whole gate to a sole reader with no other row OR. A sole shared reader must be an AND. Its partner's spare operand on column-only inputs picks out exactly the charging row's neighbors. This identifies a distinct gate outside all row ORs and their readers by domination and read order. Count that gate instead. A companion search cannot exist: the statement is about every graph of the class.

changed.title: Fixing a degree-two vertex v of a graph with no 4-cycle, where G - v and G - N[v] keep an edge, saves at least three gates at false or at least four at true
changed.statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : List (Fin n × Fin n)) (v u w : Fin n) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ e.2) → (∀ a b c d : Fin n, a ≠ c → b ≠ d → ((a, b) ∈ E ∨ (b, a) ∈ E) → ((b, c) ∈ E ∨ (c, b) ∈ E) → ((c, d) ∈ E ∨ (d, c) ∈ E) → ((d, a) ∈ E ∨ (a, d) ∈ E) → False) → u ≠ w → ((v, u) ∈ E ∨ (u, v) ∈ E) → ((v, w) ∈ E ∨ (w, v) ∈ E) → (∀ z : Fin n, ((v, z) ∈ E ∨ (z, v) ∈ E) → z = u ∨ z = w) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v ∧ e.1 ≠ u ∧ e.2 ≠ u ∧ e.1 ≠ w ∧ e.2 ≠ w) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => x e.1 && x e.2)) → (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 3 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v false e.1 && Function.update x v false e.2)) ∨ (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 4 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v true e.1 && Function.update x v true e.2))

changed.title: A row OR spare on at all its missing singleton columns, at least two, is a gate outside the row ORs and their readers for incomparable rows
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
    (r : Fin n → Fin C.gates.length) (s : Fin n → ℕ) (v : Fin n),
  let gate := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.gateAt C
  let wire := fun idx : Fin C.gates.length => n + m + idx.val
  let reads := PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.readsIn C (Finset.range C.gates.length)
  let col := fun label : Fin m =>
    List.replicate n false ++ List.ofFn (fun b : Fin m => decide (b = label))
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n + m) C →
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
  (∀ u : Fin n, C.output ≠ u.val) →
  (∀ c, ∃ u, G u c = false) →
  (∀ u w, u ≠ w → ∃ c, G u c = true ∧ G w c = false) →
  (∀ u : Fin n, reads u.val = 1 ∧ (gate (r u).val).op = .or ∧
    ((gate (r u).val).inputs = [u.val, s u] ∨
      (gate (r u).val).inputs = [s u, u.val])) →
  2 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun c => G v c = false)).card →
  (∀ c, G v c = false → (C.wires (col c)).getD (s v) false = true) →
  ∃ j : Fin C.gates.length, s v = wire j ∧
    ∀ w, j ≠ r w ∧ wire (r w) ∉ (gate j.val).inputs
changed.unlocks: one step of the general count of two gates a row on the one-a-side promise, the gate found outside the row gates; it moves no bound by itself
changed.context: On paper. A column alone gives output zero. On a neighbor of row w its OR must be off there, since turning on w changes the output through that OR. The chosen spare is on at two singleton columns, so it is a gate. If it equals a row OR or reads one by OR, the chosen row OR is on throughout that other row, contradicting row distinction by domination. If it reads a row OR by AND, that OR is on at every column missing the chosen row. Its own neighbors must then lie inside the chosen row. Equality of row indices would give a cycle in each case. Companions cannot exist: it is about every graph.
